name: f16-sim
$comment: The flyable F-16: three-axis fly-by-wire (pitch g-command with turn compensation and limiter, roll-rate command about the velocity vector, yaw damper, ARI, sideslip command) on the Stevens & Lewis airframe, trimmed at 500 ft/s, 10 000 ft, with the FMU interface of the f16-sim host as export markers. Generated by design/build_model.py; see the README.

annotations.text: **Airframe.** RigidBody3D on its principal axes (the book's Jxz tilts them 1.05 deg from the body x axis); the wrench is applied in the geometric body frame through the Mount (FixedTransform3DNeutral).
Stabilator servo: 20.2 rad/s lag, +-25 deg, +-60 deg/s (Stevens & Lewis).
Aileron servo: 20.2 rad/s lag, +-21.5 deg, +-80 deg/s (Stevens & Lewis).
Rudder servo: 20.2 rad/s lag, +-30 deg, +-120 deg/s (Stevens & Lewis).
**Inputs.** The ExportInputPass markers pass the test stimulus (globals *_amp, *_t, *_dur, throttle_set) through in bg-sim; in the FMU the host drives them.

**Three-axis fly-by-wire.** Pitch: g-command with turn compensation and the alpha/g limiter (PitchCommand, PitchFBW, Ka/Kq/Ki over qbar and Mach). Roll and yaw: LateralFBW with Kp/Kip/Kr/Kb/Kib over qbar and Mach and the ARI gain Kari over alpha. Servos: stabilator +-25 deg 60 deg/s, ailerons +-21.5 deg 80 deg/s, rudder +-30 deg 120 deg/s, all 20.2 rad/s.

options.text: 500 ft/s at 10 000 ft. The default input is a **coordinated 60 deg bank turn**: a roll-stick pulse banks the aircraft, the turn compensation pulls the 2 g and the yaw law keeps the sideslip near zero. Move the sticks, the pedals and the throttle, or switch parts of the law off.
